problems.title: Range of a linear expression
problems.question: 5<a<15,−5<b<16. Which listed value cannot equal 2a−b?
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra while keeping excluded values, and use midpoint or circle properties for geometry.
steps: The linear expression attains every value in this open interval. Among−5,34,8,0,30,−7, only −7 lies outside.

problems.title: Reciprocal data determine a squared difference
problems.question: Find(a−b)² if1/a+1/b=1.6 and 1/(ab)=0.2.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra while keeping excluded values, and use midpoint or circle properties for geometry.
formulas: ab=5 and a+b=1.6ab=8.

problems.title: A rational equation and a digit sum
problems.question: If(x²−8x)/x²=8−7x/(x−1), find the digit sum of 12x.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra while keeping excluded values, and use midpoint or circle properties for geometry.
formulas: Exclude x=0,1. Simplify to 1−8/x=1−7/(x−1).
steps: Thus 8(x−1)=7x, x=8. Then 12x=96, whose digits sum to 15.

problems.title: Trapezoid bases from a divided midline
problems.question: An isosceles trapezoid has acute angle 45°, smaller base8, and its diagonal divides the midline2:5. Find height.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra while keeping excluded values, and use midpoint or circle properties for geometry.
formulas: The two midline pieces are half the bases, so the base ratio is 2:5. The larger base is 20.
steps: Each side’s horizontal offset is(20−8)/2=6. At45°, height equals this offset, so it is 6.

problems.title: Polygon diagonals
problems.question: A convex polygon has angle sum 720°. Find its number of diagonals.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra while keeping excluded values, and use midpoint or circle properties for geometry.
formulas: (n−2)180=720 gives n=6. Diagonal count=n(n−3)/2.

problems.title: Negative exponents and prime factors
problems.question: Evaluate 8^(−9)12^(−18)16¹¹/(9¹⁰18^(−20)).
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra while keeping excluded values, and use midpoint or circle properties for geometry.
formulas: Write all bases as powers of 2 and 3. The net 2-exponent is −27−36+44+20=1; the net 3-exponent is −18−20+40=2.
steps: The result is 2·3²=18.

problems.title: Domain of a complex fraction
problems.question: For how many real x is[2−(x+3)/(x−1)]/[x+5x/(x−2)] undefined?
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra while keeping excluded values, and use midpoint or circle properties for geometry.
formulas: Inner denominators exclude1,2. The outer denominator is x(x+3)/(x−2).
steps: It vanishes at 0,−3, which must also be excluded. Four distinct values are forbidden:−3,0,1,2.

problems.title: Order negative powers
problems.question: Order A=0.25⁻¹(2/3)⁻², B=(2/5)⁻⁴, C=0.3⁻²(8/27)⁰, D=4⁻²/18⁻².
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra while keeping excluded values, and use midpoint or circle properties for geometry.
steps: Their approximate values are 9,11.111…,20.25,39.0625. Hence A<C<D<B.

problems.title: Impossible consecutive trapezoid angles
problems.question: Which consecutive-angle ratio is impossible:3:5:1:7;2:4:3:5;6:3:4:2;8:7:13:12;2:2:5:5;3:6:6:3?
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra while keeping excluded values, and use midpoint or circle properties for geometry.
formulas: The two supplementary adjacent pairs must have equal ratio sums:either first+second=third+fourth, or first+fourth=second+third.
steps: For6:3:4:2, these tests give9≠6 and 8≠7. Every other listed ratio satisfies one test.

problems.title: Bisectors at adjacent parallelogram vertices
problems.question: Bisectors from A and obtuse B meet at K. Its distance to midpoint M of AB equals the parallelogram height to AD. Find the angle between altitudes from B.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra while keeping excluded values, and use midpoint or circle properties for geometry.
formulas: Adjacent angles are supplementary, so∠AKB=90°. The midpoint of hypotenuse AB gives KM=AB/2. Height to AD is AB sin A.
steps: Thus sin A=1/2. Since A is acute, A=30°. The angle between the two inward altitude rays from B equals A, so it is 30°.

problems.title: A nested rational quotient
problems.question: Evaluate[(x−1)/(3x)] ÷ {1/(3x−6y)·[2y−x−(2y−x)/x]} at x=2025, y=−199.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra while keeping excluded values, and use midpoint or circle properties for geometry.
formulas: The bracket is(2y−x)(x−1)/x, and 3x−6y=−3(2y−x).
steps: The divisor simplifies to −(x−1)/(3x). The outer quotient is −1; the supplied values avoid all exclusions.

problems.title: When a rational expression is natural
problems.question: For how many integers n is(2n−1)/(2n)−2n/(2n−1)−1/(2n−4n²) a natural number?
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra while keeping excluded values, and use midpoint or circle properties for geometry.
formulas: On its domain n≠0,1/2, the expression simplifies to −1/n.
steps: For integer n, this is a positive integer only at n=−1, where it equals 1.

problems.title: A sum over two system roots
problems.question: The system4x²+1=y²+4x, y−x=4 has roots(x₁, y₁),(x₂, y₂). Find x₁y₁+x₂y₂.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra while keeping excluded values, and use midpoint or circle properties for geometry.
formulas: Substitute y=x+4 to obtain3x²−12x−15=0. Thus x₁+x₂=4, x₁x₂=−5.
steps: The requested sum isΣ(x²+4x)=(4²−2·(−5))+4·4=42.

problems.title: Signed distances and a midpoint
problems.question: A, B lie on opposite sides of a line at distances60,18. Find the distance from their midpoint to the line.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra while keeping excluded values, and use midpoint or circle properties for geometry.
formulas: Take signed perpendicular coordinates60 and −18. The midpoint coordinate is their average.
steps: Its distance is|(60−18)/2|=21.

problems.title: Distance from a rhombus centre to a side
problems.question: A rhombus has perimeter24 and angle 150°. Find centre-to-side distance.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra while keeping excluded values, and use midpoint or circle properties for geometry.
formulas: Side=6, height=6sin150°=3.
steps: The diagonal intersection lies halfway between parallel opposite sides, so its distance to either is 3/2=1.5.

problems.title: A possible cancellation factor
problems.question: Which listed integer can cancel from(2m+17)/(m−1)?
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra while keeping excluded values, and use midpoint or circle properties for geometry.
steps: The only possible common prime factor is 19. It occurs at m=20, giving57/19.

problems.title: Full boxes of pencils
problems.question: Distribute1010 pencils into full30- and 40-capacity boxes. How many counts of the two box types are possible?
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra while keeping excluded values, and use midpoint or circle properties for geometry.
formulas: Let counts a, b≥0. Then 3a+4b=101. Modulo3, b≡2.
steps: The possible b-values are 2,5,8,11,14,17,20,23. Each gives a nonnegative integer a. There are 8.

problems.title: Use reciprocal variables
problems.question: Evaluate[(x⁻³+y⁻³)/(x⁻²−y⁻²)+(x−y)⁻¹] ÷(x⁻¹−y⁻¹) at x=199, y=8.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra while keeping excluded values, and use midpoint or circle properties for geometry.
formulas: Put u=1/x, v=1/y. Then 1/(x−y)=−uv/(u−v), and(u³+v³)/(u²−v²)=(u²−uv+v²)/(u−v).
steps: Adding gives(u−v)²/(u−v)=u−v. Dividing by u−v gives 1. The supplied x, y avoid zero denominators.

problems.title: A circle from two perpendicular feet
problems.question: O lies inside angle A, with perpendicular feet B, C on its sides. Given∠BAO=48°, find∠ACB.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra while keeping excluded values, and use midpoint or circle properties for geometry.
formulas: ∠ABO=∠ACO=90°, so A, B, O, C lie on the circle with diameter AO.
steps: In right triangle ABO,∠AOB=42°. Angles AOB and ACB subtend chord AB, so∠ACB=42° in the intended configuration.

problems.title: A tangential midpoint parallelogram
problems.question: Joining consecutive side midpoints of a parallelogram gives a quadrilateral with an incircle. Find the ratio of adjacent original angles.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra while keeping excluded values, and use midpoint or circle properties for geometry.
formulas: The midpoint quadrilateral is a parallelogram with sides half the original diagonals. A tangential parallelogram must be a rhombus, so those diagonals are equal.
steps: A parallelogram with equal diagonals is a rectangle. Its adjacent angles are both 90°.

problems.title: Recover a reciprocal sum
problems.question: Find n+1/n if(3n²−5n+3)/(2n)=8.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra while keeping excluded values, and use midpoint or circle properties for geometry.
formulas: Multiply by 2 and group:3(n+1/n)−5=16.
steps: Thus 3(n+1/n)=21, and the requested value is 7.

problems.title: A planned speed with equal-distance halves
problems.question: A helicopter flies half its route30 km/h below plan and the other half35 km/h above plan, arriving on time. Find planned speed.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra while keeping excluded values, and use midpoint or circle properties for geometry.
formulas: Let planned speed v>30. Equal total time gives 1/(v−30)+1/(v+35)=2/v.
steps: Cross-multiplying gives v(2v+5)=2(v²+5v−1050), so 5v=2100, v=420.

problems.title: A rational equation with no roots
problems.question: Find the product of a-values for which1/(4x−6)+(2x−a)/(18−8x²)−1/(2x²+3x)=0 has no solution.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra while keeping excluded values, and use midpoint or circle properties for geometry.
formulas: The domain excludes0,3/2,−3/2. A common denominator reduces the numerator to(a−1)x+6.
steps: At a=1, the numerator is the nonzero constant6. Otherwise the root −6/(a−1) is excluded only when it equals±3/2, giving a=−3 or 5.
The product of 1,−3,5 is −15.

problems.title: Parallelogram sides from its bisectors
problems.question: A parallelogram has perimeter36. The quadrilateral formed by its internal bisectors has diagonal sum 16. Find the larger original side.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra while keeping excluded values, and use midpoint or circle properties for geometry.
formulas: If original sides are a≥b, the bisector quadrilateral is a rectangle whose diagonals both have length a−b.
steps: Thus a+b=18 and 2(a−b)=16. Solving gives a=13, b=5.

problems.title: A rectangle angle by vectors
problems.question: ABCD has AB:BC=2:3, M midpoint AB, and AK:KD=2:1 on AD. Find∠MCK.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra while keeping excluded values, and use midpoint or circle properties for geometry.
steps: CM=(−1,−3), CK=(−2,−1). Their dot product is 5 and lengths√10,√5, so cosine=1/√2.
